body:
This PR adds a one-entry thread-local front cache for repeated
`(session_id,index_id)` reader lookups. The source remains **TLS-only** at
`019868e9`; shared block-cache sharding/XXH3 and native DocID caching remain
independent work in [#5042](https://github.com/manticoresoftware/manticoresearch/pull/5042).

<!-- adaptive-experiment-20261113:start -->
**Separate adaptive-cache follow-up:** the [current opt-in experiment](https://github.com/orca-zhang/manticoresearch/blob/18a7ae4223f47fc0bda7c95d6f6be90a03fdb672/review/docid-tls/ADAPTIVE_CACHE_2026-11-13.md) adds system-mapped decoded payloads, packed small-block regions and release of fully empty regions to the OS. It includes default-versus-adaptive QPS/CPU tables and two broad/hot/broad RSS/physical-footprint diagnostics. It contains **no reader TLS** and remains outside both production PRs. The 512 MiB comparison also changes capacity; its gains are not attributed to TLS. There is **no adaptive-plus-TLS measurement**. The latest TLS evidence below remains the controlled `376fbf9`-based pair at equal block-cache budgets, alongside the original-cache dataset.
<!-- adaptive-experiment-20261113:end -->

Performance evidence now includes **both block-cache datasets**:

- **Original cache:** upstream `047d2f9` versus TLS `019868e9`, with the original
  single locked LRU and chained CRC32 in both arms.
- **Latest cache:** `376fbf9` versus the same source plus only the #5045 production
  reader diff. Both use #5042's shared LRU shards and seeded XXH3-64, common
  CI/alignment repairs and DocID budget **0** (used bytes checked as zero).

Each percentage compares TLS off/on with the **same cache implementation and
budget**. The latest block cache is benchmark context; it is not added to this
PR or a production dependency. The source contexts and measurement phases
differ, so their absolute-QPS gap is not a TLS gain and gains must not be combined.

**Added 0 / 8 / 16 MiB matrix on the latest shared block cache**

The same validated latest-context pair now covers each budget at
20k/100k/500k/1M/5M rows, with native DocID and SQL query-result caches off.
Six balanced Williams rounds x three seconds/arm, one active arm at a time,
a 30-second pre-group idle gate (mean >=90%, minimum >=80%) and continuous
one-second CPU logs keep the comparisons within each dataset group.
Every before/after cell varies only reader TLS at an equal block-cache budget:

| Rows | TLS QPS: cache off | TLS QPS: 8 MiB | TLS QPS: 16 MiB | TLS CPU/query: 16 MiB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 20,000 | +12.01% | -1.24% | +0.60% | -0.50% |
| 100,000 | +5.38% | -0.55% | -1.12% | +1.46% |
| 500,000 | -0.20% | +2.61% | +1.10% | -0.88% |
| 1,000,000 | +0.84% | +2.74% | +1.80% | -1.40% |
| 5,000,000 | +0.40% | +0.01% | +0.49% | -0.25% |

![TLS off/on and block-cache off/on are distinct comparisons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orca-zhang/manticoresearch/1ad09fe64efc3c22b4e7bb481fd89ad85c34db01/review/docid-tls/figures/reader-tls-block-cache-budgets.png)

At default 16 MiB the incremental TLS change is -1.12% to +1.80%; the
20k cache-off result is +12.01% QPS / -9.81% CPU/query. The large #5042
shared-cache implementation gains have a different denominator: for 20k,
old-to-new block cache is +127.49%, same-final-binary cache off/on is +27.17%,
and adding TLS at equal 16 MiB is +0.60%. Gains must not be combined.
With TLS on, 8/16 MiB still trail cache off at 500k/1M/5M; larger decoded
working sets may need larger budgets, which this small-budget sweep does not
rule out. Earlier 128/512 MiB cells remain in the reports separately.

Count changes are -1.11%/-0.83%/-0.78% at 0/8/16 MiB. A/A uses the TLS-on
binary at 8 MiB in both arms and gives -1.60% QPS / +1.19% CPU/query; one A/A
sample is load-flagged. No new text/count sample crosses that monitoring flag,
and all timed intervals have 100% logged coverage. This is descriptive
evidence, not a statistical confidence band or proof of isolation. No sample
is removed, and no A/A adjustment is applied. No consistent default-cache
TLS benefit is established; the earlier longer repeats remain relevant.

[Full budget tables, CPU/query, RSS, controls and exact drivers](https://github.com/orca-zhang/manticoresearch/blob/1ad09fe64efc3c22b4e7bb481fd89ad85c34db01/review/docid-tls/BLOCK_CACHE_BUDGETS_2026-11-13.md),
[updated TLS report](https://github.com/orca-zhang/manticoresearch/blob/1ad09fe64efc3c22b4e7bb481fd89ad85c34db01/review/docid-tls/TLS_REVIEW_2026-11-13.md),
[download budget evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orca-zhang/manticoresearch/1ad09fe64efc3c22b4e7bb481fd89ad85c34db01/review/docid-tls/attachments/block-cache-budget-evidence.zip).
#5045 production remains TLS-only at `019868e9`; this combined benchmark adds
no shared-cache code or native DocID code to the PR.

**Earlier longer reruns to check machine-load variation:** two independent passes,
six alternating five-second rounds/arm, fresh servers, reversed case/start order.
Every case passed a continuous 60-second idle gate (mean >=90%, minimum >=80%).
One-second host/external-process CPU logs and thermal/VM snapshots are archived.

![Reader TLS reruns with idle gates and load telemetry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orca-zhang/manticoresearch/47a856a46bb95ec3120212ed721211273014c608/review/docid-tls/figures/reader-tls-load-controlled.png)

| Rows, default 16 MiB | Rerun 1 QPS change | Rerun 2 QPS change | Rerun 1 CPU/query change | Rerun 2 CPU/query change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 20,000 | +0.28% | -0.41% | +0.93% | +0.62% |
| 100,000 | -0.20% | +1.31% | +0.23% | -1.19% |
| 500,000 | -1.68% | -0.62% | -2.54% | +0.15% |
| 1,000,000 | -1.32% | +0.14% | +1.09% | +0.04% |
| 5,000,000 | +11.33% | +0.77% | -4.36% | -0.32% |

A/A QPS changes are **-2.64% / -0.83%**;
count-control changes are -1.03% / +0.86%.
A/A runs the no-TLS binary in both labeled arms. The lowest pre-case mean idle
was 90.02%. Using the telemetry summary flag (sample-average
external CPU >10% of machine, or an interval >20%), 38/192 timed
samples are flagged; they remain in all results. External CPU means the median
of the six sample-average deltas for surviving processes outside the benchmark
process tree; short-lived external processes can be missed. These flags are
monitoring annotations, not exclusion criteria or proof of causation.

The idle gate reduces pre-existing load; these shared-workstation reruns still
have uncontrolled CPU placement/frequency and external activity.
They cannot prove what caused the previous unmonitored sign reversal.
Every new and old sample remains in the report; no A/A adjustment is applied.

The quieter second pass places all five default-cache QPS changes between
**−0.62% and +1.31%**; no default-cache sample in that pass meets the recorded
higher-load flag. Its A/A control is −0.83%. This is descriptive evidence of
small effects, not a formal noise band or confidence interval. At 1M, the fresh
passes give **−1.32% / +0.14%**, rather than the earlier unmonitored −6.53%.
The older regression remains in the record; its cause is not established.

At 5M, the first pass's **+11.33%** accompanies unequal external CPU medians
(**18.77% / 13.27%** of the machine for no TLS / TLS). It becomes **+0.77%** in
the second pass, where those CPU medians are **3.72% / 3.37%** and no sample
meets the higher-load flag. The large first-pass gain is not repeatable evidence.
By contrast, the 20k **cache-off** case gives **+6.65% / +9.07% QPS** and
**−8.70% / −6.96% CPU/query** across the two passes; the first pass is load-affected.
Cache-off gains must not be substituted for the default-cache result.

These runs do **not establish a consistent default-cache throughput benefit**.
They demonstrate real workstation-load interference and do not identify the
cause of every prior positive or negative result. No A/A subtraction is applied.

Per-sample telemetry coverage is 80.49–100%; unseen final partial intervals
cannot be declared free of interference. Raw flags and coverage are retained.

**Earlier measurements: original and latest cache contexts**

![Reader TLS with original and latest block-cache baselines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orca-zhang/manticoresearch/47a856a46bb95ec3120212ed721211273014c608/review/docid-tls/figures/reader-tls-cache-comparison.png)

**Default 16 MiB block cache, eight clients, 256 returned rows:**

| Rows | Original cache: before →TLS QPS | TLS change | Latest cache: before →TLS QPS | TLS change | Latest earlier 5-second repeat |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 20,000 | 3,419.3 →3,390.6 | -0.84% | 7,505.4 →7,447.7 | -0.77% | -1.49% |
| 100,000 | 3,034.3 →3,060.0 | +0.85% | 7,030.0 →7,066.1 | +0.51% | Not repeated |
| 500,000 | 1,452.7 →1,464.5 | +0.81% | 3,353.1 →3,427.8 | +2.23% | Not repeated |
| 1,000,000 | 1,387.3 →1,378.4 | -0.65% | 3,001.0 →3,100.5 | +3.32% | -6.53% |
| 5,000,000 | 1,252.4 →1,238.5 | -1.11% | 1,664.3 →1,712.9 | +2.92% | +0.46% |

The latest-cache gains are not consistent in longer repeats: 1M changes from
+3.32% to **−6.53%** (CPU/query +4.09%), while 5M changes from +2.92% to +0.46%.
The 20k repeat is −1.49%. A/A is +0.65% initially / -0.71% in a five-second
control added after the 1M sign reversal. No samples are discarded and no
universal default-cache benefit is established.

The full report includes both datasets at 20k/100k/500k/1M/5M rows and
0/16/128 MiB, plus 512 MiB at 5M, alongside count, point, A/A, mixed and longer
repeat cases. The 16 matched text cells use the same fixture metadata and
query-pool SHA256. Apple M4 Pro / Clang 21 `-O2 -DNDEBUG`, 128-byte rowwise stored
text, 16 KiB/LZ4, eight workers, query-result cache off. Initial cases have six
alternating three-second rounds/arm. Preselected repeats have six five-second
rounds, fresh servers and reversed starting order. Plot ranges are paired-round
ranges, not confidence intervals. All negative/control results are retained.

**Answers to the maintainer:**

1. **Default cache and larger datasets.** Both original and latest results are
   above, with all cache budgets and CPU/query data in the report. The latest
   block cache is present in both new arms; its own speedup is not attributed
   to TLS. The default-cache result is workload-dependent, and cache-off numbers
   are not substituted for default-cache evidence. There is no universal
   positive-gain or dataset-size optimum claim.

2. **Concurrent reader deletion.** Generation is invalidation, not memory
   reclamation. It does not keep an already returned pointer alive or close the
   check/use race. Arbitrary deletion during active reader use is unsafe. The
   existing session/index lifetime contract must protect that use, as it must
   after the old registry lookup releases its mutex. Shutdown requires quiescent
   callers. The tests respect these preconditions; sanitizer success does not
   prove arbitrary concurrent deletion safe.

3. **Short-lived sessions and the global counter.** Successful reader creation/
   deletion advances one process-wide atomic. Unrelated sessions can invalidate
   an entry and add coherence traffic; HTTP keepalive does not remove per-query
   docstore sessions. The latest-cache mixed tests, collected before load logging,
   use four bulk and four hot-point clients:

   - initial: total QPS +2.02%, bulk group +2.31%, hot-point group +2.00%, CPU/query -0.19%.
   - longer repeat: total QPS +1.40%, bulk group +2.51%, hot-point group +1.29%, CPU/query -1.07%.

   These measure net behavior on the latest block cache, not the isolated
   counter cost. Historical reader-hit diagnostics remain labeled as original
   cache; no old hit rate is reused as a latest-cache measurement.

The registry retains reader ownership and its 8 MiB buffer budget. TLS borrows
one key/pointer/generation entry: 32 bytes payload per OS thread on 64-bit
builds, plus runtime metadata. Coroutine migration can miss/refill without
copying buffers. Slow-path refill records generation under the registry lock;
creation also invalidates negative entries.

Both latest-context arms passed **529/529 GoogleTests** with identical eight
public reader tests. Focused ASan+UBSan and TSan each passed **11 tests ×20**
(eight reader + three block-cache cases), instrumenting docstore/fileio/tests
and reusing other engine archives, with fail-fast alignment checking. These
are focused runs, not whole-engine sanitization. The original-cache pair's
499-test/eight-reader results remain separate. The PR source retains its
original five reader tests; supplemental tests and build context are published
as review evidence. Both fresh arms use identical supported stack overrides
inherited from an earlier Clang 21 build; no fresh automatic calibration is claimed.

Updated English [two-dataset report and all tables](https://github.com/orca-zhang/manticoresearch/blob/47a856a46bb95ec3120212ed721211273014c608/review/docid-tls/TLS_REVIEW_2026-11-13.md),
[original-cache historical report](https://github.com/orca-zhang/manticoresearch/blob/47a856a46bb95ec3120212ed721211273014c608/review/docid-tls/TLS_ORIGINAL_CACHE_2026-11-13.md),
[performance documentation](https://github.com/orca-zhang/manticoresearch/blob/47a856a46bb95ec3120212ed721211273014c608/review/docid-tls/PERFORMANCE.md),
[validation](https://github.com/orca-zhang/manticoresearch/blob/47a856a46bb95ec3120212ed721211273014c608/review/docid-tls/VALIDATION.md),
[reproduction](https://github.com/orca-zhang/manticoresearch/blob/47a856a46bb95ec3120212ed721211273014c608/review/docid-tls/repro/2026-11-13/README.md),
[download latest-context evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orca-zhang/manticoresearch/47a856a46bb95ec3120212ed721211273014c608/review/docid-tls/attachments/reader-tls-latest-block-cache-evidence.zip).

These are finite hot-query pools on a shared workstation, without controlled
CPU affinity/frequency or a formal confidence interval. They do not establish
Linux SQL throughput, cold-storage behavior, production capacity, query-cache
efficiency or safety outside the existing lifetime contract. Neither PR depends
on the other; no production source was changed in this evidence update.
title: perf: cache docstore reader lookups in thread-local storage
